blocks.text: Every reaction inside your cells leaves a residue. Break down protein and you get poisonous ammonia; respire glucose and you get carbon dioxide. If these piled up unchecked you would be dead in hours. Four organs work continuously to keep that from happening.

blocks.markdown:
## Three words that are easily confused

**Excretion** is the removal from the body of the waste products of metabolism — substances made inside the cells that would be harmful if they accumulated. Urea, carbon dioxide and excess salts are excretory products.

**Egestion** (defaecation) is the removal of undigested food as faeces. This material was never absorbed into the cells, so it is not a metabolic product at all.

**Secretion** is the release of a useful substance made by a gland for a purpose — saliva, bile, insulin, sweat's cooling function. A secretion is wanted; an excretion is not.

blocks.title: Deamination
blocks.text: The removal of the amino group from an excess amino acid in the liver. The amino group becomes ammonia, which is immediately converted to the far less toxic urea; the remainder of the molecule is used for energy or stored. This is where nearly all urea comes from.

rows: Urea, excess water, excess mineral salts
As urine through the ureter, bladder and urethra
Water, mineral salts, a little urea
As sweat from the sweat glands
In bile, into the gut and out in faeces
blocks.caption: The four human excretory organs. The kidney is the most important; the liver makes urea but the kidney removes it.

blocks.markdown:
### Excretion in other organisms

Simple and small organisms have simpler solutions, because their surface area to volume ratio is high enough for diffusion alone to work.

- **Amoeba** — carbon dioxide and ammonia diffuse out across the cell surface membrane; excess water is expelled by a contractile vacuole.
- **Paramecium** — the same, with two contractile vacuoles.
- **Earthworm** — a pair of **nephridia** in nearly every segment, each opening to the outside through a pore.
- **Insects** — **Malpighian tubules** attached to the gut. They excrete uric acid as a near-dry paste, which conserves water.
- **Fish** — the gills excrete ammonia directly into the surrounding water; freshwater fish also pass large volumes of dilute urine.
- **Flowering plants** — oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse out through **stomata** and **lenticels**; water vapour leaves by transpiration; other wastes such as tannins, latex, resins, gums and alkaloids are stored in leaves, bark or heartwood and shed with them.

items: Mammals excrete nitrogen as urea, which is soluble and needs a moderate amount of water to flush away.
Birds, insects and reptiles excrete uric acid, which is almost insoluble and needs very little water — a real advantage for an egg-laying animal or a flying one.
Bony freshwater fish and aquatic invertebrates excrete ammonia, which is highly toxic but is diluted instantly by the surrounding water.

blocks.title: Classifying a process as excretion, egestion or secretion
blocks.prompt: Decide whether each of the following is excretion, egestion or secretion, and give your reason: (i) carbon dioxide leaving the lungs, (ii) faeces leaving the rectum, (iii) bile entering the duodenum, (iv) sweat on the skin.

steps.text: Carbon dioxide is produced by respiration inside every cell and is toxic if it accumulates, so removing it is excretion.
Faeces consists mainly of undigested cellulose, dead gut cells and bacteria. This material was never taken into the cells and is not a metabolic product, so its removal is egestion.

Bile is manufactured by the liver for a purpose: it neutralises acid and emulsifies fat. Producing it is therefore secretion — although the bile pigments within it are genuinely excretory, which is why this case is a favourite examination question.

Sweat is a mixed case. Its water and salts are excess materials being removed, which is excretion, but sweating also serves the deliberate purpose of cooling the body, which is secretion. State both if a question asks.

blocks.answer: (i) Excretion. (ii) Egestion. (iii) Secretion, although the bile pigments it carries are excretory. (iv) Both — excretion of water and salts, and secretion for the purpose of cooling.

blocks.title: The liver and the kidney work as a pair
blocks.text: The liver produces urea by deaminating excess amino acids. The kidney filters that urea out of the blood. Damage to the liver means ammonia builds up; damage to the kidney means urea builds up. Knowing which organ does which is worth several marks.

blocks.title: Never call faeces an excretory product
blocks.text: This is one of the most heavily penalised errors in WAEC Biology. Faeces is egested, not excreted, because it was never part of the body's metabolism. The excretory product that leaves in faeces is the bile pigment, not the food residue.

points: Excretion removes metabolic waste; egestion removes undigested food; secretion releases a useful product.
The human excretory organs are the kidneys, lungs, skin and liver.
Urea is formed in the liver by deamination of excess amino acids and removed by the kidneys.
Amoeba uses a contractile vacuole, the earthworm nephridia, insects Malpighian tubules, and fish their gills.
Plants excrete gases through stomata and lenticels and store solid wastes in tissues that are later shed.
